index.meta_title: Table Copy - One-Click Copy Web Tables to Excel, No More Messy Formatting
index.meta_description: Say goodbye to messy formatting! Table Copy is a lightweight bookmarklet that lets you copy any web table (including those made with divs) to Excel, CSV, or JSON with one click. No installation needed, perfect formatting.

index.hero_h1:
Copy Any Web Table,
as Easily as Copying Text.
index.hero_slogan: Ditch the tedious screenshots and manual entry. One click to grab data to your clipboard for a perfect paste.
index.why_title: Like You, We Were Tired of the Tedium
index.why_p: We are data enthusiasts and heavy users of productivity tools. For countless days and nights, needing to get data from web pages into Excel, we were tormented by broken formatting, hidden `<div>` tables, and slow extensions. We believed there had to be a better way. And so, 'Table Copy' was born. It's not bloated software, just a pure, fast, and focused tool designed to solve one problem: elegantly copying web tables.

index.features_title: One Tool for All Your Needs
index.feature1_p: Supports not only traditional `<table>` elements but also intelligently recognizes modern tables built with `<div>` layouts (based on ARIA standards).
index.feature2_p: Our unique Rich Text (HTML) copy feature writes the table structure to the clipboard, ensuring a perfect, format-preserving paste into Excel, WPS, or Notion.
index.feature3_p: Copy as Rich Text, TSV, CSV, or JSON. Export directly to a CSV file (perfect for Excel) or even copy the table's raw HTML source code to meet all your needs.
index.feature4_p: It's just a bookmarklet. No installation, no background processes, ready when you are. All operations are performed locally in your browser. We never see, send, or store any of your data.
index.feature5_p: Save the table as a PNG image with one click. Perfect for sharing in presentations, reports, or on social media. What you see is what you get.
index.use_case1_p: Quickly extract data tables from financial statements and industry reports online without waiting for IT support, and start your analysis immediately.
index.use_case2_p: Easily grab competitor product prices, sales volumes, and specifications to create comparison sheets and inform your marketing strategy.
index.use_case3_p: Efficiently collect data from Wikipedia, academic sites, and government reports for papers and research, significantly boosting your literature review productivity.
index.faq1_q: Is this tool safe? Will it upload my data?
index.faq1_a: Absolutely safe. Table Copy is a 100% client-side tool. All data recognition and processing happens locally in your browser. Nothing is ever sent to or stored on any server.
index.faq2_q: How is it different from a browser extension?
index.faq2_a: It's a 'bookmarklet,' which is much lighter than an extension. No installation from an app store, no background resource usage. Click to use, and it's gone when you're done. Of course, this also means it can't perform complex background tasks like scheduled scraping, which extensions can.
index.faq3_q: Does it work on all websites?
index.faq3_a: It supports the vast majority of tables using standard `<table>` tags or ARIA-compliant `<div>` structures. For pages built with extremely complex or non-standard frontend frameworks, it might not work perfectly. We are continuously improving the algorithm.
index.faq4_q: Is this tool free? Will it cost money in the future?
index.faq4_a: Yes, the current bookmarklet will always be free. We believe good tools should be widely accessible. In the future, we might release a more powerful paid browser extension (e.g., with multi-page scraping, scheduled tasks), but the core functionality you see today will always be free.
index.community_p: If you find this tool useful, share it with your friends! For feedback and ideas, connect with us.
index.footer_p: © 2025 Table Copy. Powered by Gemini AI.

feature_list: Full Page Capture: Uses `html2canvas` to capture the entire HTML document, handling modals and overlays for a clean output.

web-to-image.pdf_promo: Need searchable and selectable text? Use our: Web to PDF Converter.
web-to-image.about_title: About this tool (How it works & EEAT)
web-to-image.about_p1: Implementation & Maintenance: This tool is maintained by the TableCopy team. The core capture logic uses the popular `html2canvas` library, with added robustness through failure prompts and fallback mechanisms.
web-to-image.about_p2: Technical Details: The script temporarily hides its own modal to avoid self-capture and uses `useCORS` to improve the rendering success rate of cross-origin image resources. The image is exported via a dataURL to trigger a browser download.
web-to-image.about_p3: Trustworthiness & Auditability: The project is a static code repository. All logic can be reviewed in `tools/tablecopy/`. Third-party dependencies are loaded from a CDN; for offline deployment, the script can be bundled and hosted from a trusted source.
web-to-image.faq_q1: What if the capture includes unwanted pop-ups or toolbars?
web-to-image.faq_a1: The script attempts to hide its own UI. For third-party elements like chat widgets or cookie banners, please close them manually or hide them using browser developer tools before capturing.
web-to-image.faq_q2: Why are some images or resources missing from the exported image?
web-to-image.faq_a2: If a resource is from a third-party domain and lacks the proper CORS headers, the browser will block it from being drawn to the canvas, causing it to be missing from the exported image. Solutions include opening the page in an incognito/new tab to allow resources to load, or saving key images locally first and then compositing the screenshot.
web-to-image.faq_q3: How can I get a higher resolution or smaller file size?
web-to-image.faq_a3: To increase resolution, adjust the `scale` parameter (e.g., `window.devicePixelRatio * 2`), which increases pixel density but also significantly increases memory usage and processing time. To reduce file size, use an image compression tool after exporting (like TinyPNG) or lower the quality parameter before exporting from the canvas (for JPEGs).
web-to-image.faq_q4: How to avoid memory crashes when processing long pages?
web-to-image.faq_a4: Capturing large pages can consume a lot of memory. It's recommended to capture in sections (splitting into multiple images) or reduce the `scale`, then merge the images locally. Another strategy is server-side rendering/capturing, but this comes with privacy risks.
web-to-image.faq_q5: How can I provide feedback or contribute improvements?
web-to-image.faq_a5: We welcome you to submit an issue or PR in our GitHub repository (path: `tools/tablecopy/`). Please provide a reproducible example page or a screen recording to help us locate the issue and perform regression testing.
web-to-image.faq_footer: Need searchable text or better print quality? Go to: Web to PDF or return to the Homepage.
